title: Sprint status reads origin/main and gives done/total, percent, next, what is left and an honest ETA
goal: kbmon.py --status sprints reads the sprint items from the local origin/main ref through git (bl_view.items_at) with no fetch; for each active or planned sprint it prints the state, done/total and percent (done and dropped count as done), the doing and todo counts, the next item and the open items by title, beside the host load; it gives an ETA of the open items times the median interval between the sprint's last 5 done commits on origin/main, called an estimate that names the median and the count it rests on; it prints how many commits the checkout is behind origin/main; a backlog id is printed only on a line where the operator acts; the sprint panel's data carries the same source, behind count and done-commit times, so --from-snapshot gives the same answer

gates.question: The main checkout often lags origin/main by hundreds of commits. Where does sprint status read the items?
options: the local origin/main ref through git, no fetch inside kbmon, with a line saying how many commits the checkout is behind
fetch origin first, bounded by the timeout, then read origin/main
the checkout's own files, with a behind-by line
gates.recommendation: the local origin/main ref through git, no fetch inside kbmon, with a line saying how many commits the checkout is behind
gates.answer: the local origin/main ref through git, no fetch inside kbmon, with a line saying how many commits the checkout is behind

gates.question: What does a sprint's ETA rest on?
options: the open items times the median interval between the sprint's last 5 done commits (throughput, so parallel workers count)
the open items times the median claim-to-done time of the sprint's last 5 items
gates.recommendation: the open items times the median interval between the sprint's last 5 done commits (throughput, so parallel workers count)
gates.answer: the open items times the median interval between the sprint's last 5 done commits (throughput, so parallel workers count)

gates.question: Where origin/main cannot be read (no such ref, no repository), what does the sprint panel read?
options: the checkout's own item files, source checkout, no behind count and no done times (so no ETA)
no sprint rows: the panel is an error
gates.recommendation: the checkout's own item files, source checkout, no behind count and no done times (so no ETA)

gates.question: Which commits give a sprint's done times for the ETA?
options: the first-parent commits whose subject starts 'chore(backlog): done ID' for an item of the sprint, at their commit time, the newest per item
every commit that touches a done item's file
gates.recommendation: the first-parent commits whose subject starts 'chore(backlog): done ID' for an item of the sprint, at their commit time, the newest per item
gates.answer: the first-parent commits whose subject starts 'chore(backlog): done ID' for an item of the sprint, at their commit time, the newest per item

notes: Plan 2026-10-19: premise on a planted clone whose checkout lags origin/main by 3 done commits: the sprint panel counts 0 done (todo 5, doing 1) while origin/main holds 3 of 6 done; --status sprints exits 2. Done commits are first-parent commits whose subject starts 'chore(backlog): done ID'. With fewer than 2 done commits the answer says there is no ETA yet. The check's figures: done at 10:00, 10:20, 10:40, so the median is 20 min and 3 open items give about 60 min.
